sector: A volunteer-run weekend farmers market in a municipal park, free to the public, funded by daily stall fees.
founded_place_size: Founded 2016, in a park in Burlington, Vermont. Volunteer-run, 36 to 44 stalls, open weekends May through October.
about: Cedar Commons is a neighbourhood farmers market that runs on weekends in a Burlington park, free to walk into and funded entirely by the vendors who pay a daily stall fee. It has outgrown its chalkboards and its bedsheet banner. The signage exists to get families to the right lot, past the entrance and to the stall they are looking for, printed cheaply and well at a local sign shop.
audience: Neighbourhood families and weekend walkers who arrive on foot or park in the wrong lot, plus the vendors and volunteers who run the morning. Read from a moving car and from across a field.
price_positioning: A free public market funded by 25 to 60 dollar daily stall fees, often part-donated. Everything prints on coroplast and vinyl at a local sign shop. Flat inks and heavy type, never a refined tint palette that would be unreadable outdoors and would make a free market look like it is charging.

palette.name: Meadow Green
palette.role: mandatory wherever the stacked wordmark is set, and on every stall sign
palette.usage: CEDAR and COMMONS in the stacked wordmark, the green double square of the signature move; the trader name and the rule on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; other type on Sign White; a solid panel carrying Sign White type; or the single ink of the recovered mark.

palette.name: Barn Red
palette.role: mandatory wherever the stacked wordmark is set
palette.usage: The 10 mm rule the stacked wordmark sits on. Otherwise only small accents such as arrows; never a ground, a panel or body text.

palette.name: Harvest Gold
palette.usage: Small accents only, such as an arrow or a dot. Never a ground, a panel or type on Sign White: signage is read from a moving car and from across a field.

palette.name: Sign White
palette.role: mandatory ground on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; the ground behind the stacked wordmark wherever it is set
palette.usage: The ground of every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf, and the ground the stacked wordmark sits on; type reversed out of a Meadow Green or Cedar Ink panel. Not used in market-mark.svg, whose background stays transparent.

palette.name: Cedar Ink
palette.role: mandatory for the stall number on every stall sign
palette.usage: The stall number on every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf; dates, directions, listings and fine print on Sign White; a solid panel carrying Sign White type; or the single ink of the recovered mark.

typography: Cedar Commons runs on two families. The name is Bodoni Egyptian Bold at 180 pt on 190 pt for a poster, stacked CEDAR above COMMONS, each line tracked out individually until the two measure exactly the same width, and the whole block set on a 10 mm Barn Red rule; the same lockup drops to 96 pt on 104 pt for a stall trader and 56 px on 60 px on screen, and it is never set on one line. Wayfinding is Interstate Bold at 60 pt on 66 pt, tracking +0.01 em. Listings and board copy are Interstate Regular at 18 pt on 24 pt, tracking 0, held to 65 characters a line. Fine print is Interstate Regular at 12 pt on 16 pt, tracking +0.03 em, and nothing sets smaller than that outdoors. Flat inks throughout, no tints.
voice: Warm, plain and welcoming, like a volunteer at the gate. Example line: "Cheerful, legible from a distance, few colours, and it lives outdoors in the rain. Not precious. Tell us what our mark can and cannot do."
brand_assets_status: The market mark was drawn nine years ago by a volunteer's cousin, who is not reachable, and screen-printed onto aprons and tote bags. No file of any kind was ever kept. The best surviving copy is a photograph of one apron folded on a picnic table. There is no vector art, so the mark has to be recovered from that photograph rather than redrawn.
values: Community and thrift. Recover the real mark rather than replace it, keep the set to a few flat inks that print cheaply, and tell the committee what the mark can and cannot do before they pay for plates.

scale.tracking: set per line, roughly +0.02 to +0.12 em, until CEDAR and COMMONS measure the same width
scale.note: Always stacked, CEDAR above COMMONS, on a 10 mm Barn Red rule. Same behaviour at the stall trader size, 96 pt on 104 pt, and on screen at 56 px on 60 px.
Wayfinding only. Bodoni Egyptian carries the name, Interstate carries the directions.

scale.sample: Free to walk in, every Saturday from May through October.
scale.note: Stall listings and board copy, flat ink on coroplast.

scale.sample: Daily stall fees 25 to 60 dollars. Ask a volunteer at the gate.
scale.note: Smallest size the market sets. Nothing goes below this outdoors.

type_system.signature_move: The wordmark is always stacked, CEDAR above COMMONS, each line tracked out until both measure exactly the same width, the block sitting on a 10 mm Barn Red rule, so it reads as a green double square underlined in red before it reads as words.
rules: Never set the name on one line. CEDAR always sits above COMMONS.
Track each line of the wordmark individually until CEDAR and COMMONS measure exactly the same width.
The stacked block always sits on a 10 mm Barn Red rule.
Bodoni Egyptian Bold carries the name only. Wayfinding and listings are Interstate.
Flat inks only, never a refined tint palette, because it has to print cheaply on coroplast and vinyl and stay readable outdoors in the rain.
Signage is read from a moving car and from across a field, so nothing sets smaller than the 12 pt fine print step.

palette_rules.distribution: Sign White #FBFAF5 is the ground of every stall sign, as on cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf, and the ground behind the stacked wordmark wherever it is set. Meadow Green #3F7D44 or Cedar Ink #23301F may be a solid panel carrying Sign White type; Barn Red #B23A2E and Harvest Gold #E0A526 are never a ground or panel. The stacked CEDAR COMMONS wordmark is Meadow Green on a Sign White ground, on its 10 mm Barn Red rule. Other type on Sign White is Cedar Ink or Meadow Green. Every stall sign keeps the colours of cedar_commons_plate_card.pdf: Sign White ground, Cedar Ink stall number, Meadow Green rule and trader name. The recovered mark is one flat ink, Cedar Ink or Meadow Green, in market-mark.svg and wherever it is placed, as the cedar_commons_apron.jpg print is a single dark green ink. Beyond the wordmark rule, Barn Red and Harvest Gold are small accents, such as arrows, together no more than 5% of the designed area.
palette_rules.opacity: Flat inks throughout, no tints. Every palette colour prints solid, at 100%, with no tint, screen, halftone, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode, because it has to print cheaply on coroplast and vinyl. No scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph.
palette_rules.forbidden: No refined tint palette and no tint or screen of any ink; no metallic, foil or gloss effect, Harvest Gold included, which prints as a flat ink; no Harvest Gold type on Sign White. No colour outside the five palette hexes, #3F7D44, #B23A2E, #E0A526, #FBFAF5 and #23301F, for type, grounds, panels, rules, arrows, icons or the recovered mark.
palette_rules.photography: Photographs keep their own corrected colour and are never recoloured toward the palette. No colour sampled from a photograph, such as the canvas of cedar_commons_apron.jpg, is used for type, grounds, panels, rules or the recovered mark. cedar_commons_site_info_tent.jpg, shot in warmer light than the other site frames, is brought to the same morning look as cedar_commons_site_entrance.jpg and cedar_commons_site_vendor_row.jpg, not warmed or tinted toward Harvest Gold.
